Rashi on Megillah 9b:11:1.hebrew: הא לכל דבריהן זה וזה שוין - ואם בא להקטיר או לעבוד שום עבודה, משמש בשמונה בגדים כהן שעבר ככהן המשמש:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:11:1.english: Thus, with regard to all their [other] matters, this [one] and that [one] are equal - And if he comes to burn incense or to perform any [Temple] service, the former [High] Priest serves in eight garments, like the serving [High] Priest:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:11:2.hebrew: כל מצות כהונה גדולה עליו - משמש בח' בגדים, לא פורע ולא פורם, ומצווה על הבתולה, ומוזהר על האלמנה, ומקריב אונן:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:11:2.english: All of the mitzvot of the High Priesthood [are incumbent] upon him - He serves in eight garments, does not let his hair grow long and does not rend [his garments in mourning], is commanded regarding [marrying] a virgin, is warned against [marrying] a widow, and offers sacrifices [even] while an onen [a mourner prior to burial]:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:11:3.english: And he is not fit - to serve neither in eight garments as a High Priest nor in four [garments] as a common priest:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:14:1.english: [The Mishnah] is [according to] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] - and he stated it anonymously in accordance with his own view:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:14:2.hebrew: ונסיב ליה אליבא דתנאי - במרובה בגדים סבר לה כרבנן, ובכהן שעבר סבר לה כר' מאיר:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:14:2.english: And he formulates it according to [different] tanna'im - With regard to [a High Priest consecrated by] multiple garments, he holds in accordance with the Rabbis, and with regard to a [High] Priest who has stepped down, he holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Megillah 9b:15:1.hebrew: אין בין במה - אין הפרש בשעת היתר הבמות בין במה גדולה — זה מזבח של משה בעודו בנוב וגבעון:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:15:1.english: There is no [difference] between an altar - There is no difference, during the time when [private] altars were permitted, between a great altar — that is, the altar of Moses while it was in Nob and Gibeon:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:15:2.hebrew: לבמה קטנה - מזבח של יחיד, שכל יחיד ויחיד עושה במה לעצמו:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:15:2.english: To a small bamah [altar] - An altar of an individual, for each and every individual makes a bamah for himself:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:15:3.english: Is sacrificed on an altar - a small [altar]:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:15:4.english: Any [offering] that is not vowed or contributed, etc. - In [tractate] Zevachim, [the Gemara] derives this in the last chapter:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:16:1.hebrew: פסחים ותו לא - והא קתני סיפא: "כל שאינו נידר ונידב אינו קרב בבמה קטנה", ואילו בגדולה היו מקריבין קרבנות צבור — תמידין ומוספין; וקא ס"ד דאף חובות צבור שאין קבוע להן זמן היו קריבין בה, כגון פר העלם דבר של צבור ושעירי ע"ז:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:16:1.english: Paschal offerings and nothing more? - But doesn't the latter clause [of the Mishnah] teach: "Anything that is neither vowed nor donated [as a freewill offering] is not offered on a minor bamah," whereas on a major [bamah] they would offer communal offerings — daily offerings and musaf offerings; and [the Gemara] initially assumed that even communal obligations that do not have a fixed time were offered on it, such as the bull for an unwitting communal transgression and the goats for idolatry:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:16:2.english: Similar to Paschal lambs - And all obligatory [offerings] that have a fixed time, like Paschal lambs:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:17:1.hebrew: מני - מתניתין דקתני דבמה קטנה אין קרב בה שום חובה, ואמר דבמה גדולה לא עדיפא מינה אלא בחובות הקבוע להן זמן:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:17:1.english: Whose [opinion is] - our Mishnah, which teaches that on a small altar no obligatory [offering] is sacrificed, and states that a great altar is not superior to it except regarding obligatory [offerings] that have a fixed time:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:17:2.hebrew: ר' שמעון היא - דאמר בפרק בתרא דזבחים: אף צבור לא הקריבו בבמה גדולה שום חובה, אלא פסחים וחובות הקבוע להן זמן; אבל חובות שאין קבוע להן זמן, כגון פר העלם דבר ושעירי ע"ז, הכא והכא לא קרב. אבל כדרבנן דהתם לא מתוקמא מתניתין, דהא אמרי: כל שהצבור מקריבין באהל מועד שבמדבר, מקריבין באהל מועד שבגלגל, דהיא במה גדולה — ואפילו פר העלם דבר; ומתניתין קתני: פסח וכיוצא בהן:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:17:2.english: It is Rabbi Shimon - For he says in the last chapter of Zevachim: Even the congregation did not sacrifice on a great bamah any obligatory offering, except Paschal lambs and obligatory offerings for which there is a set time; but obligatory offerings for which there is no set time — such as the bull for a matter hidden [from the congregation] and the he-goats for idolatry — were sacrificed neither here [on a small bamah] nor here [on a great bamah]. However, our Mishnah cannot be established in accordance with the Rabbis there, for they say: Anything that the congregation sacrifices in the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness, they sacrifice in the Tent of Meeting in Gilgal, which is a great bamah — and even the bull for a matter hidden [from the congregation]; whereas our Mishnah teaches: the Paschal lamb and the like:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:18:1.hebrew: בכל הרואה - בכל מקום שיוכל לראות משם את שילה, ובפרק בתרא דזבחים יליף טעמא:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:18:1.english: In any place that overlooks [it] - In any place from which one can see Shiloh, and in the last chapter of [tractate] Zevachim [the Gemara] derives the reason [for this]:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:1:1.hebrew: לא חמד אחד מהם נשאתי - שלא יאמר: "חמור לא לקח, אבל חפץ אחר לקח":
Rashi on Megillah 9b:1:1.english: I have not taken one item of value [ḥemed] from them - so that [one] would not say: "A donkey he did not take, but another item he did take."

Rashi on Megillah 9b:1:2.hebrew: להאיר לכל העמים - שאם לא כן, יאמר בן נח: מותר בע"ז; ומדרשו (ע"ז נה.): להחליקן בדברים כדי לטורדן מן העולם:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:1:2.english: To give light to all the nations - For if not [for this added word], a Noahide would say [that he is] permitted [to engage] in idolatry; whereas its midrashic exposition (Avodah Zarah 55a) [is that the verse's unemended wording means] to entice them with smooth words in order to banish them from the world:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:2:1.hebrew: אשר לא צויתי לעובדם - שאם לא כתבו "לעובדם", משמע "אשר לא צויתי" שיהיו, ויאמר: א"כ אלהות הן, שעל כורחו נבראו:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:2:1.english: Which I have not commanded to serve them - For if they [the Elders] had not written "to serve them," it would imply "which I have not commanded" that they exist, and one would say: "If so, they are deities, for they were created against His will."

Rashi on Megillah 9b:3:1.hebrew: וכתבו - במקום "ואת הארנבת", "ואת צעירת הרגלים", לפי שידיה קצרות וקטנות מרגליה:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:3:1.english: And they wrote - in place of "and the hare," [they wrote] "and the short-legged one," because its forelegs are shorter and smaller than its hind legs:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:5:1.hebrew: יפיותו של יפת - הוא לשון יון, לשונו יפה משל כל בני יפת:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:5:1.english: The beauty of Japheth - [this refers to] the Greek language, [whose] language is more beautiful than [that of] all the descendants of Japheth.

Rashi on Megillah 9b:6:1.hebrew: מרובה בגדים - כהנים ששימשו בבית שני, ואף בבית ראשון מימות יאשיהו ואילך, שנגנז צלוחית של שמן המשחה:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:6:1.english: [One consecrated by] multiple garments - [This refers to the High] priests who served in the Second Temple, and also in the First Temple from the days of Josiah onward, when the flask of the anointing oil was hidden away:

Rashi on Megillah 9b:6:2.hebrew: פר הבא על כל המצות - כהן משיח שהורה היתר בדבר שזדונו כרת, ועשה כהוראתו, מביא פר, שנאמר: "אם הכהן המשיח יחטא לאשמת העם" וגו' (ויקרא ד׳:ג׳):
Rashi on Megillah 9b:6:2.english: The bull that comes for any of the mitzvot - An anointed [High] Priest who ruled [something to be] permitted in a matter whose intentional [transgression incurs] karet [excision], and acted in accordance with his ruling, brings a bull, as it is stated: "If the anointed priest shall sin so as to bring guilt on the people," etc. (Leviticus 4:3):

Rashi on Megillah 9b:7:1.hebrew: כהן המשמש - כגון שאירע בו פסול ומינו אחר תחתיו, ועבר פסולו וחזר לעבודתו והעבירו הבא תחתיו — הראשון קרוי "משמש", והשני "עבר":
Rashi on Megillah 9b:7:1.english: The serving [High] Priest - For example, where a disqualification occurred to him and they appointed another in his place, and [then] his disqualification passed and he returned to his service and they removed the one who came in his place — the first is called "serving," and the second [is called] "former":

Rashi on Megillah 9b:7:2.hebrew: אלא פר יוה"כ - שאי אפשר להביא שנים, וכן עשירית האיפה — חביתי כהן [גדול] שבכל יום — שאי אפשר להביא שנים:
Rashi on Megillah 9b:7:2.english: Except for the bull of Yom Kippur - because it is impossible to bring two [of them]; and similarly, the tenth of an ephah — the chavitin [griddle-cake offering] of the [High] Priest [brought] every day — because it is impossible to bring two [of them]:

Tosafot on Megillah 9b:13:1.hebrew: ולא לכהן הדיוט משום מעלין בקדש וכו' - קשיא: למה ליה האי טעמא? תיפוק ליה דכיון דראוי לכהן גדול, אי לאו משום איבה, א"כ אינו יכול לשמש בארבעה בגדים משום דהוה ליה מחוסר בגדים. ויש לומר דמשום האי טעמא לא היינו מקפידין, כיון דעל פי בית דין הוא, אי לאו טעמא דמעלין:
Tosafot on Megillah 9b:13:1.english: Nor as a common priest, because one elevates in [matters of] sanctity, etc. - It is difficult: why does [the Gemara] need this reason? Let it derive [from the fact] that since he is fit [to serve] as a High Priest — were it not for [the concern of] hatred — if so, he cannot serve in [the] four garments [of a common priest], because he would be [considered] lacking garments. And one can say that because of that reason we would not be particular, since it is by the authority of the court, were it not for the reason of "one elevates [in matters of sanctity]":

Tosafot on Megillah 9b:17:1.hebrew: מני רבי שמעון היא דאמר אף צבור לא הקריבו - נראה דכיון דמוקמינן למתני' כרבי שמעון, א"כ סיפא נמי אתיא כוותיה, דקתני: "זה הכלל, כל הנידר ונידב קרב בבמה". וקשה, דהא נזירות דהוי דבר הנידר ונידב, כדאמרינן בפרק שני דתמורה (דף יד: ושם), ואפילו הכי אית ליה לר' שמעון פ' בתרא דזבחים (דף קיז. ושם) דמנחות ונזירות אין קרב אפילו בבמה גדולה! וי"ל דהכי מיפרשא מתניתין: זה הכלל, כל הנידר ונידב שקרב בבמה גדולה — כגון עולה ושלמים ליחיד — קרב בבמה קטנה; וכל שאינו נידר ונידב, ואע"פ שקרב בבמה גדולה, אין קרב בבמה קטנה, אבל מודה הוא דיש נידר ונידב שאין קרב לא בבמה גדולה ולא בבמה קטנה:
Tosafot on Megillah 9b:17:1.english: According to whose opinion is it? It is Rabbi Shimon, who says: Even the public did not sacrifice - It appears that since we establish the Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, if so, the latter clause also accords with him, as it teaches: "This is the general rule: anything that is vowed or donated is offered on a bamah." And this is difficult, for Nazirite [offerings] are something that is vowed or donated, as we say in the second chapter of Temurah (14b, and there), and even so, Rabbi Shimon holds in the last chapter of Zevachim (117a, and there) that meal-offerings and Nazirite [offerings] are not offered even on a great bamah! And one can answer that the Mishnah is explained thus: "This is the general rule: anything that is vowed or donated" — [meaning] that is offered on a great bamah, such as a burnt-offering and peace-offerings of an individual — "is offered on a small bamah"; and anything that is not vowed or donated, even though it is offered on a great bamah, is not offered on a small bamah; however, he concedes that there is [an offering that is] vowed or donated that is offered neither on a great bamah nor on a small bamah:

Tosafot on Megillah 9b:6:1.hebrew: אין בין כהן משוח למרובה בגדים אלא פר הבא על כל המצות - פירוש: פר כהן משיח שחטא בשוגג, דעשה אחת מכל מצות ה' אשר לא תעשינה ואשם בדבר שזדונו כרת. אבל לא מיירי בפר העלם דבר של צבור, דכתיב ביה "הכהן המשיח" (יחטא), דהא מרבינן בת"כ ואפילו כהן הדיוט יכול להביאו, וכל שכן מרובה בגדים:
Tosafot on Megillah 9b:6:1.english: There is no difference between an anointed priest and one [consecrated] with multiple garments except the bull that comes for all the mitzvot - Meaning: [this refers to] the bull of an anointed priest who sinned unwittingly — who committed one of all the mitzvot of the Lord that are not to be done, and incurred guilt — regarding a matter whose intentional violation [carries the penalty of] karet. However, [the Mishnah] is not speaking of the bull for an unwitting communal sin, regarding which it is written "the anointed priest" (shall sin), for we derive an inclusion in Torat Kohanim [to teach] that even an ordinary priest can bring it, and all the more so one [consecrated] with multiple garments:

Tosafot on Megillah 9b:7:1.hebrew: אין בין כהן המשמש לכהן שעבר אלא פר יום הכפורים - קשה: אמאי נקט "לכהן שעבר"? דהא אפילו ביום שאירע בו פסול לכהן המשמש ושמש זה תחתיו, הוי חילוק זה, שהפר בא מן המשמש אע"פ שאין משמש, כדאי' בירושלמי; ואם כן, הוה ליה למימר "בין הכהן המשמש לכהן שיעבור"! וי"ל, דאי נקט "לאותו שיעבור", הוה משמע: הא לאותו שעבר כבר, דהוי בכל שנה, יש הרבה חילוקים ביניהם; משום הכי נקט "לאותו שעבר", לאשמועינן דאף בדידיה ליכא אלא חילוק זה. וא"ת: למאי דפרישית שהפר הוי מאותו שאירע בו הפסול אע"ג שאין משמש, א"כ קשיא מהא דאמר סוף פ"ק דשבועות (דף יד:): "אשר לו", ולא משל אחיו הכהנים — ואדרבה, היה לו לומר: ולא מאותו המשמש תחתיו, דהוי רבותא טפי! ושמא משום דהוי מלתא דלא שכיחא שבקיה, ונקט מידי דשכיח כל שנה. וההיא נמי דהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף יט.) דקאמר דגלי רחמנא שחיטה בבעלים, לא קשה לפירושינו דשרי; דכיון דזכי ליה רחמנא, הוי כאילו מקדיש משלו:
Tosafot on Megillah 9b:7:1.english: There is no difference between a serving [High] Priest and one who has passed [from office] except the bull of Yom Kippur - It is difficult: why did [the Mishnah] state "to [a High] Priest who has passed"? For even on the day when a disqualification occurred to the serving [High] Priest and this [other one] served in his stead, this distinction [already] applies, for the bull comes from the [regular] serving [High Priest] even though he is not [currently] serving, as stated in the Yerushalmi; and if so, it should have said "between the serving [High] Priest and the [High] Priest who will pass [from office]"! And one can answer that if it had stated "to that one who will pass," it would have implied that for the one who has already passed — which occurs every year — there are many differences between them; therefore it stated "to that one who has passed," to teach us that even in his case there is only this difference. And if you ask: according to what I explained, that the bull is from the one to whom the disqualification occurred even though he is not serving, if so, it is difficult from what [the Gemara] says at the end of the first chapter of Shevuot (14b): "[the bull] which is his" — and not from his brother priests; on the contrary, it should have said "and not from the one serving in his stead," which would be a greater novelty! [One can answer that] perhaps because it is an uncommon occurrence it left it aside, and stated something that is common every year. And that [passage] as well in [the chapter] HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 19a), where [the Gemara] says that the Merciful One revealed [that] slaughter [must be] by the owner, is not difficult for our explanation, for it is permitted; since once the Merciful One granted him ownership, it is as if he consecrates from his own:
